utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-12-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Could I have the appearances, please. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Kenneth Scott for the Prosecution. I'm joined today by Ms. Josee D'Aoust and also our case manager Ms. Denise Gustin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KOSTA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. Counsel Doris Kosta, co-counsel appearing for Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Rajic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand. I'm not getting any interpretation in my headset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question: Can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you have anything to complain?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I ask for leave to address you at a later point with issues dealing with my Defence. As for the conditions in the Detention Unit, I have no complaints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will come to you at a later stage. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference in accordance with the Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and the purpose of this hearing is to assist the parties to facilitate the preparation of the case, and there are several items on my agenda. The first issue is the disclosure issues. Mr. Scott, has the Prosecution complied with the obligation of disclosure under Rule 66(A)(i) since January 2004?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Yes. As I explained to your senior legal officer this morning in a 65 ter meeting, the Prosecution believes that we have complied with all discovery obligations to date. Of course the Rule 68 obligation is a continuing one, which we understand, but subject to that continuing disclosure obligation, we believe that all disclosure is current at the present time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could I get confirmation from the Defence on that disclosure issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. KOSTA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as we said this morning, it's true that we have received documents from the Prosecution, and we agree that they continue to act pursuant to Article 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The next issue is about agreed facts. Are there any proposals from the side of the Prosecution concerning the agreed facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, very briefly, a report on that. You will recall, Judge Liu, that in approximately August of last year the Prosecution provided to Mr. Olujic approximately 200 proposed facts for agreement. Unfortunately and for various reasons, there were delays in receiving a response to those proposals. However, on approximately the 18th of March of this year we did receive a response from Mr. Olujic in which he responded to each of the 200 facts, agreeing to some, agreeing -- in toto, agreeing in part to some, and disagreeing with others. Since that time we have had approximately two meetings and various telephone conversations with Mr. Olujic where some progress has been made but we're still not -- haven't finalised that. And as I reported this morning, we do anticipate spending quite a bit of time on that with counsel in the immediate future, and in fact, since counsel's in town, we expect to sit down and speak with her tomorrow on this matter. So nothing more specific -- well, there is more progress than there has been in the past, because we did receive a response, but it's still being worked on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your information. This matter has been on our agenda for quite a long time, and I hope both parties could meet together and to reach agreement on certain facts as early as possible. So I hope that the parties could arrive at an agreement in a month's time, at least before the summer recess. Yes. The next issue will be the pre-trial briefs. Mr. Scott, when do you think you are in a position to submit your pre-trial briefs?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we can realistically do that just prior to the summer recess, which I understand starts in approximately the last week of July this year, I believe, but if we could have right up until that time, I think that's realistic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. And how about Defence? When do you think you're in the position to file your pre-trial brief?

utterances.speaker: MS. KOSTA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that depends on when we receive the Prosecution pre-trial brief, but in accordance with what we said today during the Pre-Trial Conference, I can say that we can do this by the end of September. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Just for the information of the parties, we might have four Trial Chambers available ready to hear any cases which is ready. So I hope that both parties be prepared for the trial of this case at the end of this year or at the very beginning of the next year. So the most important thing is to have the filings from the both parties, the pre-trial briefs. Of course, other preparation should also be undergoing at this moment. Mr. Scott, would you please brief me how big that case will be in terms of the witnesses and the documents. You may just give me a rough idea, of course, at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Well, I'm happy to report we think we can probably do it in a little shorter time than the Milosevic case. I think we can do better, a little better than that. But I think that realistically we're looking at about 30 live witnesses, approximately, and 20 whatever you would like to call them, 92 bis or paper witnesses. Those numbers could be modified, depending, again, on the agreed facts, or possible adjudicated facts could come into that. For example, if there were to be adjudicated facts on the issue of international armed conflict, that could reduce the number of witnesses. But roughly speaking -- and I must say, Your Honour, when I did this with Mr. Harhoff this morning, these were very rough estimates. It's not something we specifically looked at just recently, but I think it's a ballpark estimate. So 30 live and 20 on paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any other matters concerning the preparation of the case at this stage? I see none. Could I turn to Mr. Rajic. I believe that you have something to say to me at this stage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I wish to assist the work of the Court, the Prosecution, and my Defence. With respect to the response to these 200 facts, I have given my precise instructions and told everything I know to my counsel, Attorney Zeljko Olujic. He proceeded to work and this, but at a later stage I discovered that he had not followed my instructions faithfully, or the facts that I told him. Therefore, I think that the document delivered by him is factually inaccurate in many respects, and there are matters there I cannot agree with. I think that whether intentionally or unintentionally, my defence Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. has been obstructed. I have informed the Office of the Prosecutor of this, and I asked my attorney to come so that we could clarify this. I asked that he attend this Status Conference so that this matter can be clarified. However, he has not shown up. For this reason, I conclude that certain problems have arisen in my relations with my Defence counsel. I will try to solve them, but I have no way of doing that until he comes to The Hague. My co-counsel, Ms. Doris Kosta, is unable to communicate with me, and for this reason I am not receiving legal aid. That is all I wish to say at present, Your Honour, and I hope that with your many years of legal experience you can assist me and help me with your advice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Generally speaking, the communications before the accused and his counsel should be kept confidential. I believe that is the principle in the Rules. Anyway, we quite understand the situation you are in at this moment. I'm very much worried about the preparation of this case because of that relationship between you and your lead counsel. Ms. Kosta, would you please inform me why Mr. Olujic was not able to come for this Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MS. KOSTA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I am aware, Your Honour, he has to appear in court in Croatia. I believe that this is also a reflection of the situation that has obtained over the past month between Mr. Rajic and Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And when do you think that Mr. Olujic will be here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MS. KOSTA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next week he should be here. As our client has been persistently asking for a meeting with him, I will ask him to travel here at once, especially as we have outstanding matters to discuss with the Prosecutor's office as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Please convey my words to him that his client is in need of him in The Hague for some very important matters of this case. Thank you. Are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise at this stage? Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you very much. I mean, we're also quite concerned about the situation and which was only fully appreciated by us today based on conversations with counsel who is here, who has been quite helpful in this respect. But of course we're very concerned because it raises all sorts of uncertainties as to who -- who to deal with and who has authority to speak for Mr. Rajic at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Kosta?

utterances.speaker: MS. KOSTA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did inform all those present at the Rule 68 ter [as interpreted] meeting this morning about the situation. I believe that at present I am able to protect the interests of our client, Mr. Rajic. I will do my best to have Mr. Olujic travel to The Hague and have a meeting with the accused. It is true that a problem has arisen, and I have drawn attention to it this morning. Since June, I have not been able to have telephone contacts with Mr. Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What's the reason for that problem? Can you shed some light on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KOSTA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in May last year, I was away from my office. I was not in the city of my residence. I do not know when my client will call me on the phone and make use of the privileged telephone line. On the day that he called, his wife happened to be in my office. My intern very recklessly and in ignorance of the Rules of The Hague Tribunal and the Detention Unit said to him, "Well, here's your wife," and he said to her, "Your husband is on the phone," and they greeted each other on the phone. I was not aware of this. I do not know how this came to light, because we have received guarantees that our telephone conversations with our client are not listened into. We did not intend to abuse the privileged telephone line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, to my understanding, the privileged telephone line is for the accused and his counsel only. It should not be misused or abused. I believe there must be a reason for that, and that bar could be lifted if the accused is sure that he will never abuse this privilege. If the accused would like to do so, he could file something, application, to the Registrar and to see what they could do to it. I believe that this matter is entirely in the mandate of the Registrar. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MS. KOSTA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree with Your Honour. We have already or, rather, my colleague Mr. Olujic has already applied to the Registry. We have apologised. And this was not an intentional abuse of the privileged telephone line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Anyway, we'll see to it. Yes, Mr. Rajic, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you for your suggestion, and here in front of you I wish to promise that no line will be abused. Should such a thing happen, I fully agree to have all my communications cut off. However, this was truly unintentional. I give my word in front of all these people here and Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that I'll send the transcript to the Registrar and let him read your views on it. And I also hope Ms. Kosta could send this transcript to the lead counsel, Mr. Olujic, on those matters. Well, I believe that's all for this Status Conference. The hearing is adjourned.
